intro: Numbers to PDF converts Apple Numbers spreadsheets into PDF so anyone can see your tables without a Mac, iPhone or iPad. It is handy for sending a budget, an inventory or an expense sheet made in Numbers to someone who works on Windows, or for printing it from another computer.

LibreOffice imports the file on our server, with no internet connection, and exports it as a spreadsheet. The import is partial: Numbers places tables, charts, images and text boxes freely on a canvas, whereas a classic spreadsheet is a grid, so tables usually arrive with their values, but the layout, charts and styles may change or be lost. Each PDF comes with a notice so you can check it.

If a wide table is split across several pages, turn on "Excel: each sheet on a single page" under more options: each sheet will take up a single PDF page, sized to its content. You can also choose PDF/A-2b or PDF/UA, limit the result with the Pages field, for example "1, 4-6", and set the quality and maximum resolution of images.

For an exact result, the best option is to export from Numbers with File > Export To > PDF; if you would rather keep working with the data, export to Excel and use Excel to PDF. Several files can be uploaded at once: each gives its own PDF and, when there is more than one, a ZIP too. The page limit depends on your plan.

faq.q: Why is a chart missing from the PDF?
faq.a: Numbers charts are not always imported. If you need it, export the PDF from the app itself or paste the chart as an image before converting.

faq.q: Can I convert an Excel file?
faq.a: Yes, with Excel to PDF, which accepts XLSX and XLS and usually gives a more faithful result because LibreOffice knows Microsoft's format better.

faq.q: What about Pages or Keynote documents?
faq.a: There are Pages to PDF and Keynote to PDF, which use the same LibreOffice import and give the same quality notice.
